segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen who live as temporary residents of the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through being made holy by the Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ: May grace and peace be multiplied to you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who in his great mercy has caused us to be born anew into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in the heavens for you,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who are being guarded by God’s power through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In this you rejoice, though now for a little while, if it must be, you have been grieved by various trials,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that the tested genuineness of your faith—more precious than gold, which perishes even though it is tested by fire—may be found to bring praise and glory and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Though you have not seen him, you love him; though you do not see him now, you believe in him and rejoice with a joy that is beyond words and filled with glory,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: as you receive the outcome of your faith, the salvation of your souls.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was about this salvation that the prophets who prophesied of the grace meant for you sought and searched intently,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: searching to find what time or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ within them was pointing to in testifying beforehand to the sufferings destined for Christ and the glories that would follow them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you in these things, which have now been announced to you through those who brought you the good news by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—things into which angels long to look.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Therefore, having dressed your minds for action and keeping sober, set your hope fully on the grace being brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As children of obedience, do not conform to the desires you once had in your ignorance,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but, as the one who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in your whole way of life,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for it is written,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “You shall be holy, because I am holy.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And if you call on as Father the one who judges impartially according to each person’s work, live in fear throughout the time of your stay as foreigners,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: knowing that it was not with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were ransomed from the empty way of life handed down by your ancestors,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or spot.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was foreknown before the foundation of the world but was made manifest at the end of the times for the sake of you

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Having purified your souls by obedience to the truth so as to have sincere brotherly love, love one another earnestly from the heart,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for you have been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers and the flower falls,

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: but the word of the Lord endures forever.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And this is the word that was announced to you as good news.

notes.note: The word describes someone staying for a time in a place that is not their home, without implying banishment, which “exiles” now suggests. The Septuagint uses it of Abraham among the Hittites. Scholars debate whether Peter describes his readers’ actual social standing, their spiritual condition as people whose home is elsewhere, or both.

This was the established term for Jews living scattered outside the land of Israel. Peter applies it to communities in five Roman provinces of Asia Minor (modern Turkey) that, judging from the rest of the letter, included many non-Jews. The readers are being addressed in Israel’s own vocabulary.

notes.phrase: for obedience and sprinkling with the blood of Jesus Christ
notes.note: The image recalls Exodus 24, where the people pledge obedience and Moses sprinkles them with the blood of the covenant. The Greek leaves open whether “of Jesus Christ” belongs only to the blood or also to the obedience (“obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling with his blood”).
The Greek is plural here, a Semitic turn of phrase for God’s dwelling that most translations flatten to “heaven.” The plural is kept where the Greek has it; in verse 12 the Greek is singular.

“In this” most likely refers to the whole prospect described in verses 3–5, but the Greek could also mean “in him” (God or Christ) or “at that time,” that is, the last time. The verb can also be read as a command, “rejoice,” though most take it as a statement.
Older versions have “temptations,” but the word here means hardships that put faith to the proof, not enticements to sin. Most modern translations already use “trials” in this verse.

notes.phrase: what time or what kind of time
notes.note: The first Greek pronoun can be read with “time,” as here, or on its own as “whom,” giving “what person or time,” which several major translations adopt. Both are grammatically sound and scholars are divided. The reading chosen keeps the focus on timing, which the following words about sufferings and later glories develop.

“Gospel” has become a religious term and a book title. The Greek verb was an ordinary one for announcing good news publicly, and many modern translations already alternate between “gospel” and “good news.”

notes.phrase: having dressed your minds for action
notes.traditional: gird up the loins of your mind
notes.note: The Greek is literally “having girded up the loins of your mind.” The picture is of tucking a long robe into the belt so as to move freely for work or travel. It may echo the Passover instruction in Exodus 12:11 to eat with loins girded, ready to depart. Most modern translations also replace the idiom with an equivalent such as “prepare your minds for action.”

The adverb “fully” stands between two verbs in Greek and could go with either. Most translations attach it to hoping, as here; a number of scholars attach it to the preceding word, giving “keeping perfectly sober, set your hope.”

Many manuscripts read “from a pure heart,” and many translations follow them; the Greek text translated here has the shorter reading. The evidence is closely balanced, and other critical editions print “pure” in brackets. Some later manuscripts also add “through the Spirit” after “obedience to the truth.”

notes.phrase: the living and enduring word of God
notes.note: The Greek word order allows “living and enduring” to describe either the word or God (“the word of the living and enduring God”). Most translators take it of the word, because the quotation that follows says that the word of the Lord endures.

notes.phrase: “All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of grass. The grass withers and the flower falls,
notes.note: The quotation is Isaiah 40:6–8 in a form close to the Greek Septuagint. “All flesh” is a Hebrew way of saying all humankind in its frailty. The passage opens Isaiah’s announcement of good news to exiles, and Peter picks up that theme in the next verse.

candidates.reason: Recurs with πάροικος/παροικία (1 Pet 1:17; 2:11; Heb 11:13; Eph 2:19; Acts 7; 13:17), and translations vary among exiles, strangers, sojourners, aliens and foreigners; the pair needs a fixed, distinct set of renderings.
Frequent in 1–2 Peter and found in Paul, Hebrews and James; versions vary among conduct, behavior, way of life and (KJV) conversation, and the cognate verb ἀναστρέφω should match.
The λύτρον word group (λυτρόω, λύτρον, λύτρωσις, ἀπολύτρωσις) runs through the Gospels, Paul, Hebrews and 1 Peter, and the choice between “ransom” and “redeem” should be uniform.

Occurs in Romans, 1 Thessalonians, Hebrews and 1–2 Peter; translators differ among brotherly love, mutual love and love for brothers and sisters, and the choice bears on how ἀδελφός language is handled.
Very common across the New Testament and rendered variously as lusts, passions, desires or cravings; a decision is needed on a default and on when a negative coloring is warranted.

warnings: Verse 21: πιστός is not rendered with a register form (faithful / believing) and has no register-exception note.
